issues.translation_quote: I thought I'd buy my wife a fur coat.
issues.justification: The Russian means he intended to spend the money on a fur coat instead of taking the trip; in context this is fine, but later the exchange implies this as a comic motive for not going. However the larger problem is that the surrounding subtitle sequence is handled too literally and loses the rhythm of the joke. A more idiomatic phrasing like 'I was going to buy my wife a fur coat instead' would preserve the setup better.

issues.source_quote: Ну что же это такое... - Ну разве можно!...
issues.translation_quote: Oh! What is this... - How can you!...
issues.justification: This famous comic moment depends on the reporter's embarrassed fluster and the family's indignant interruption. 'How can you!' is stilted and fails to sound like natural spoken English. The joke lands weakly; something like 'Really now!' or 'Honestly!' would better preserve the comic social awkwardness.

issues.translation_quote: No-need... Go...
issues.justification: This is not meaningful English. The source is comic broken speech ('не надо' distorted), but the translation should produce understandable comic broken English, not a malformed calque. As written, the line is effectively untranslated and obscures characterization.

issues.translation_quote: touryst
issues.justification: The misspelled transliteration reproduces Russian pronunciation visually, but in English subtitles this looks odd and distracts. A more functional way to render the comic accent would be preferable.

issues.translation_quote: That's not topical! "The Island of Bad Luck"!
issues.justification: 'Not topical' is unnatural in English and misses the comic register. The point is 'that's not the thing' / 'that's not in fashion' / 'that's not relevant now.' The joke's timing suffers from the stiff phrasing.

issues.translation_quote: Ugly on the outside, kind within
issues.justification: Comprehensible, but a bit flat and literal. 'Hideous to look at, kind underneath' or similar would better preserve the song's playful rhythm and tone.

issues.translation_quote: Russo Turisto! Obliko Morale! Verstehen? Russo Turisto... Obliko Morale... Verstehen?
issues.justification: The phrase is iconic mock-macaronic comedy. Repeating it twice in the subtitles where the source only presents it once as the punch dulls the joke, and leaving it entirely untranslated gives no help to viewers unfamiliar with the film. Some support like 'Soviet tourist—moral character, understand?' would preserve the humor and meaning.

issues.translation_quote: An injury—everything believable!...
issues.justification: 'Достоверно' here means 'convincing/realistic/authentic,' not merely 'believable.' The line is about staging a fake injury realistically. The rendering weakens the criminal-plan context and the comic fixation on realism.

issues.translation_quote: Passed out. Woke up in a cast.
issues.justification: This catchphrase is central and recurs throughout the film. 'Woke up in a cast' is understandable, but it loses the abrupt clipped comic rhythm of 'came to — cast!' A sharper recurring English hook was needed for consistency and humor.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, в нашем деле гланое - этот самый реализм!
issues.translation_quote: As our dear boss says, in our line of work the main thing is realism!
issues.justification: The source has comic criminal pomposity plus malapropistic flavor. The translation is semantically correct but too plain, missing the pompous mock-professional tone that makes the line funny.

issues.source_quote: Товарищи, внимание! Сейчас у вас свободное время.
issues.translation_quote: Comrades, attention! You now have free time.
issues.justification: This sounds like a literal announcement, not natural tour-guide English. Since Soviet institutional speech is part of the film's period flavor, the translation should preserve the formal bureaucratic comic tone in idiomatic English, e.g. 'Comrades, attention! You now have some free time.'

issues.source_quote: Инкэс... тиора пэн? [Но где же он?]
issues.translation_quote: Inkes... tiora pen? [But where is he?]
issues.justification: The made-up foreign gibberish is correctly glossed, but elsewhere many surrounding invented-language lines are left only transliterated and partly garbled, with inconsistent handling. Since the glosses are the only meaningful content, the transcription errors and inconsistency reduce comprehensibility in a plot-critical scene.

issues.translation_quote: Really a severe sprain
issues.justification: Awkward English word order. 'A really bad sprain' would sound natural and fit spoken dialogue better.

issues.translation_quote: Gipso srakh nibedyu... [he even lost consciousness...]
issues.justification: The source implies 'he even passed out'; 'lost consciousness' is acceptable, but in this fast comic scene the formal medical phrasing is less effective than colloquial English.

issues.source_quote: Товарищ, товарищ, товарищ, хорошо бы ай-лю-лю, цигель, цигель - время, товарищ!
issues.translation_quote: Comrade, comrade, comrade, it'd be good to— ai-lyu-lyu, zigel, zigel—time, comrade!
issues.justification: This is a famous line and a comic high point. The translation is nearly uninterpretable English, so the punchline fails. The meaning is roughly 'Less ai-lyu-lyu, more zigel-zigel — time's up!' and needs an idiomatic comic solution.

issues.source_quote: Да меня... меня же будут спрашивать, что с рукой?
issues.translation_quote: But they'll... they'll ask me what's wrong with my arm! Then you say: Slipped. Fell. Closed fracture. Passed out. Woke up in a cast. Slipped... Closed fracture... cast!
issues.justification: The translation inserts and rearranges material confusingly. It creates a broken sequence ('Slipped... Closed fracture... cast!') that does not track the source cleanly and makes the mnemonic joke less effective.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: Such is "c'est la vie," as they say...
issues.justification: The joke is that he parrots a foreign phrase with naive prestige. 'As they say over there' would better preserve the provincial comic effect than the neutral 'as they say.'

issues.source_quote: Если человек идиот - то это надолго.
issues.translation_quote: If a man is an idiot, it's for a long time!
issues.justification: The literal wording is intelligible, but the recurring punchline needs an idiomatic, quotable form. 'If someone's an idiot, that's a life sentence' or similar would better carry the comic sting. As translated, it sounds clunky and repeatedly lessens one of the film's signature lines.

issues.translation_quote: amateur performances / amateur antics
issues.justification: The same Russian term is translated differently in nearby contexts, and both choices miss the Soviet-specific flavor. In one case it refers to amateur artistic performance; in another, to unauthorized initiative. Better contextual adaptation or distinct idiomatic solutions are needed to preserve both meaning and Soviet-era register.

issues.translation_quote: Topic: "New York—City of Contrasts."
issues.justification: This is accurate, but the deadpan absurdity would be stronger with a more natural spoken setup, e.g. 'Your lecture topic is...' The current phrasing reads like a written program note.

issues.source_quote: Отлично, отлично, скромненько, но со вкусом...
issues.translation_quote: Excellent, excellent— modest, but tasteful...
issues.justification: This famous phrase is wooden in English. The comic faux-gallant tone is weakened; 'simple, but tasteful' is the established idiomatic equivalent and would preserve the line better.

issues.translation_quote: C-cr... [crap]
issues.justification: The gag is that he starts to say something but suppresses it. 'C-cr...' does not correspond to any natural start of 'crap' in English and feels arbitrary. The censoring joke is lost; a better solution would recreate a broken-off vulgarity naturally in English.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: May you live... on nothing but... your salary!
issues.justification: This iconic curse is culturally loaded and comic precisely because it sounds absurdly petty in Soviet conditions. The literal rendering communicates denotation but not the force or humor. It needs a more pointed equivalent or at least sharper phrasing to land.

issues.source_quote: А у нас... Управдом - друг человека!
issues.translation_quote: But here... the building manager is man's best friend!
issues.justification: The joke is understandable, but 'building manager' is bland and fails to carry the specific Soviet social figure of the 'управдом.' The comic bite and local color are reduced.

issues.source_quote: Такого возьмём без шума и пыли!
issues.translation_quote: We'll take this one easy—no noise, no dust!
issues.justification: Literal and understandable, but 'no fuss, no muss' or another idiom would better preserve the jaunty criminal patter.

issues.translation_quote: his broad
issues.justification: This captures vulgarity, but 'broad' sounds American and period-marked in a way that may not suit the overall register. A less regionally marked colloquial insult might fit better.

issues.translation_quote: With a light flick of the wrist, the trousers transform... The trousers transform... Transform, the trousers do... into elegant shorts.
issues.justification: The phrase is famous for its escalating comic repetition and the suit/pants mishap. The Yoda-like 'Transform, the trousers do' is a serious misfire and sounds unintentionally bizarre rather than theatrically comic.

issues.translation_quote: but that's not эстетично...
issues.justification: The Russian word is left in Cyrillic inside an English sentence. This is untranslated material in a key comedic exchange and clearly a translation failure.

issues.source_quote: Ребята, на его месте должен быть я. Напьёшься - будешь!
issues.translation_quote: Guys, I should have been in his place! — Get drunk enough, and you will be!
issues.justification: The line is understandable, but 'get drunk enough, and you will be' is stiff. A snappier comeback would better preserve the joke's rhythm.

issues.source_quote: Наши люди в булочную на такси не ездят!
issues.translation_quote: Our people don't take taxis to the bakery!
issues.justification: This iconic line is translated literally, but without context it sounds merely odd. It needs a more pointed colloquial rendering to preserve its aphoristic comic force in English.

issues.translation_quote: marked on the diagram with the letters "M" and "F."
issues.justification: This is incorrect. The Russian letters refer to 'М' and 'Ж' (male/female), not M and F. Using 'M' and 'F' changes the visual joke and the spoof-military precision of the briefing.

issues.translation_quote: in the заданном direction
issues.justification: Part of the Russian is left untranslated. This is a clear translation error that breaks immersion in the middle of an important exposition scene.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a whole ticket pack, win... a tractor rack!
issues.justification: The source is a rhyme-joke and slogan parody. 'Tractor rack' is semantically off and not funny. The wordplay fails to cross into English, which is a major style loss under the instructions.

issues.translation_quote: Browse the комиссионки
issues.justification: The key noun is left untranslated. This is a straightforward untranslated-material error in a plot-relevant instruction.

issues.translation_quote: Give me one live round!
issues.justification: Semantically close, but the humor comes from his naive eagerness and the official-sounding mismatch. 'Give me one real bullet' would sound more natural and funnier in context.

issues.translation_quote: the client will be fine
issues.justification: This is slightly awkward criminal slang in English. 'He'll be ready' or 'he'll be ripe' would better suit the scene.

issues.translation_quote: Why'd you shave your mustache, dummy?
issues.justification: The line is iconic and comic. 'Dummy' is weak and unnatural here; the blunt absurdity of the original is undercut. A stronger colloquial choice is needed for the joke to land.

issues.source_quote: Будете у нас на Колыме - милости просим! Нет уж, лучше вы к нам!
issues.translation_quote: Well, if you're ever in Kolyma... — No, better you visit us!
issues.justification: The dark joke hinges on Kolyma's connotations and the deadpan response. The translation is literal but fails to help the target viewer grasp why it's funny; the cultural joke largely falls flat.

issues.source_quote: А под дичь водку не пьют!
issues.translation_quote: You don't drink vodka with game!
issues.justification: Too flat for a punchline. The source is mock-connoisseur bluster; a more idiomatic line like 'Vodka with game? Never!' would preserve the comic pretension better.

issues.translation_quote: Down with drunkenness!
issues.justification: This slogan-like phrase should sound like a mock-official campaign motto. The literal translation is understandable but clumsy and less punchy than the Russian satirical slogan.

issues.translation_quote: Elements of the sweet life...
issues.justification: Literal and somewhat awkward. 'Signs of the high life' or similar would sound more idiomatic in English while preserving the insinuating tone.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: In the morning, champagne is drunk only by aristocrats and degenerates.
issues.justification: The wording is stiff and unquotable. This famous line needs a sharper, idiomatic form to preserve its punch and comic contrast.

issues.source_quote: Будет тебе там и ва-анна, будет и кофэ, будет и какава с чаем...
issues.translation_quote: You'll get your ba-ath there, and your coff-ey, and cocoa with tea too...
issues.justification: The joke plays on affected pronunciation and class pretension. 'Ba-ath'/'coff-ey' are awkward visual distortions that do not produce a natural English comic effect.

issues.translation_quote: A шикарный plan, boss!
issues.justification: The adjective is left untranslated. This is a clear untranslated-material error in a short but important line.

issues.translation_quote: Just one 'tab-LEHT' will do.
issues.justification: The source jokes with a foreign accent, but the transcription trick in English is opaque and unnatural. It neither translates the meaning elegantly nor recreates the joke effectively.

issues.translation_quote: To our случайное acquaintance...
issues.justification: The Russian adjective is left untranslated in a visible English sentence. This is a clear translation failure.

issues.source_quote: Не виноватая я! Он сам пришёл!
issues.translation_quote: Twasn't my fault! He came here on his own!
issues.justification: The line is intelligible, but 'Twasn't' gives it an archaic or dialect flavor not present in the original. A more natural colloquial English line would better suit the melodramatic parody.

issues.translation_quote: You must обязательно meet your friend.
issues.justification: The adverb is left untranslated. This is an obvious untranslated-material error in an important plot instruction.

issues.translation_quote: as always—a taxi
issues.justification: Slightly awkward in English. The intended meaning is 'we'll send the usual taxi' or similar.

issues.translation_quote: I see—a drinking buddy!
issues.justification: Meaning is conveyed, but the sharp accusatory comic snap is softened. 'So you're his drinking pal' or an equally barbed colloquialism would better preserve character voice.

issues.translation_quote: stomp back to your pad
issues.justification: This is a jarring mixture of registers: Russian criminal slang becomes dated American slang. It shifts character voice and locale in an intrusive way.

issues.source_quote: к жене приедете как огурчик, без гипсу, без пыли, без шуму
issues.translation_quote: you'll come to your wife like a cucumber, no cast, no dust, no noise
issues.justification: 'Like a cucumber' is a literal calque of the idiom 'fresh as a cucumber' / 'right as rain.' The line sounds absurd in the wrong way and misses the jaunty criminal idiom.

issues.source_quote: куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: Strike while the iron is hot—right at the cash register!
issues.justification: The line is a comic blend of two sayings. The literal translation is understandable but not funny in English; the hybrid proverb joke does not land. A creative equivalent is needed.

issues.translation_quote: what do you see on the highway? Report.
issues.justification: The translation misses the spoof-police-radio flavor. 'What do you see on the highway? Report' is serviceable but wooden, and elsewhere radio chatter is inconsistently rendered, reducing style cohesion.

issues.translation_quote: Hands... up! Both!...
issues.justification: The source contains comic mangled speech ('обои' instead of 'оба'). The translation normalizes part of it and loses the speech-joke. A playful broken-English equivalent could preserve the humor.

issues.source_quote: Как говорил один мой знакомый, покойник: Я слишком много знал...
issues.translation_quote: Like one acquaintance of mine used to say— now dead: "I knew too much..."
issues.justification: Accurate in meaning, but too explanatory and flat. The source is a crisp black-humor line; the English lacks the same punch and rhythm.

issues.translation_quote: we'll all land it
issues.justification: This is awkward and unclear. The source means roughly 'we'll all get caught/go down together' in dialectal speech. The translation obscures the line's meaning.
